newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver close lower on fresh selling.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver close lower on fresh selling.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carats closed five rupees lower at 4,660 rupees per 10 grammes due to sluggish seasonal demand while improved arrivals and a setback in the world market prompted fresh selling.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 50 rupees lower at 54,550 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Wednesday.
** Silver (.999) closed five rupees lower at 6,795 per kg after opening steady at 6,800 rupees per kg. A weak trend in the world market prompted selling by local stockists.
Gold 24 carats closed five rupees lower at 4,660 rupees per 10 grammes on Thursday as fresh arrivals and a weak world trend prompted selling by local stockists, dealers said.
Gold was down 15 rupees per 10 grammes on Wednesday.
Dealers said supplies of gold smuggled by sea had also been rising ahead of the four-month June-September monsoon season which had just arrived in the southern state of Kerala.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 50 rupees lower at 54,550 rupees per piece. Biscuits lost 200 rupees on Wednesday.
Silver (.999) closed five rupees lower at 6,795 rupees per kg on a weak world trend after a steady start.
Dealers said they expected gold to move in a narrow range and silver to extend losses on Friday. (Conversion $1=35.80 rupees)
